articles.title: Hugging Face CEO calls for ‘radical transparency’ after ‘unprecedented’ OpenAI hack
articles.summary: "The first autonomous agent cyberattack is an unprecedented event. It deserves an unprecedented response!"
articles.full_text:
In Brief Posted: 9:33 AM PDT · July 26, 2026 Anthony Ha Hugging Face CEO calls for ‘radical transparency’ after ‘unprecedented’ OpenAI hack After OpenAI recently admitted that one of its models had breached the systems of AI platform Hugging Face , Hugging Face’s CEO Clem Delangue posted on X that he was flying to San Francisco to have “a little chat with that ‘rogue agent.’” Then, in a follow-up post on Saturday, Delangue outlined what he’d asked for from OpenAI.

He said he called for “radical transparency,” asking OpenAI to “release the traces from the ‘rogue’ agents so the entire research community can study what happened.” And he also wants “more capabilities for defenders,” calling for OpenAI to commit $100 million worth of computing power “to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models.” Delangue added, “The first autonomous agent cyberattack is an unprecedented event.

It deserves an unprecedented response!” Despite the autonomous nature of the attack, cybersecurity experts suggested that it could also be blamed on human error — namely, OpenAI’s apparent failure to properly configure what should have been a fully isolated testing environment.

When asked about Delangue’s comments, an OpenAI spokesperson confirmed that the meeting took place and pointed to a company post that said, “This is an unprecedented incident, and we think it marks an important moment for AI safety.

We are still conducting a thorough review along with external advisors and with oversight from our Safety and Security Committee.

Once the review is complete, we plan to publish a technical report of our learnings in the coming weeks.” This post has been updated with a comment from OpenAI.

articles.title: Bluesky’s AI assistant Attie expands into an open social research tool
articles.summary: Users can now ask Attie questions about news, trends, and conversations on Bluesky and other apps on the AT Protocol.
articles.full_text:
Attie , Bluesky’s AI assistant that lets you build custom social feeds without programming, is evolving into an open-ended research tool.

The company this week said it’s added a new feature to the AI assistant, called Quests, that lets users ask it for information and news spreading across the broader Bluesky social network, nicknamed the Atmosphere.

This includes not only Bluesky, but also any app that integrates with the underlying AT Protocol.

Bluesky’s user growth has slowed over the past eight months — the social network saw its user base double to 40 million last October, within just a year, but it now reports around 45.6 million registered accounts .

So the company has been looking to develop tools and services that could allow it to grow its user base and potentially monetize it.

Attie, launched in March , is a separate product by Bluesky that lets users design their own algorithm, create custom feeds, and, one day possibly, vibe-code their own apps.

While the AI assistant is free for the time being, the company has toyed with the idea of charging for the service.

Quests adds new capabilities to Attie, allowing users to ask it open-ended questions to research what’s happening on this part of the open social web.

For instance, you could ask Attie to pull information about trending topics, or help you identify the most influential accounts in a particular field or location, the company explained. “Attie’s AI is a tool that helps you make sense of the internet, helping you fight back against the proliferation of misinformation and noise by giving you the tools to find the truth yourself,” wrote Bluesky’s chief innovation officer Jay Graber, who stepped down in March from her role as CEO of the company . (She’s since been replaced by Toni Schneider, the former founding CEO of Automattic.) “Our bet is that tools that help people make sense of the world will prove to be more useful than those that fill it with confusion,” Graber wrote. “We want Attie to reduce the barrier to entry and expertise required to learn how to use the AT Protocol, and to put the tools for customizing your experience in the hands of anyone who wants them.” Graber noted Attie is being redesigned to add accessibility features and a new logo, and more changes are coming in the months ahead.

For now, the new Attie experience is in beta, and users will be invited in from a waitlist over the coming weeks.

While many Bluesky users tend to dislike AI for economic, political, and environmental reasons, the company has had to balance its community’s leanings with the need to generate revenue to help itself and the AT Protocol development it leads remain afloat.

In March, Bluesky said it had raised $100 million in funding  in a round that closed in 2025.

That gives it runway to experiment with ideas like Attie and how AI can play a role in the Atmosphere, as well as with other services, like a premium subscription or tools for power users.

articles.title: OpenAI’s new voice mode makes it to the ChatGPT desktop app
articles.summary: ChatGPT Voice on desktop can work with both ChatGPT Work and Codex to complete tasks and control agents.
articles.full_text:
In Brief Posted: 6:36 AM PDT · July 24, 2026 Ivan Mehta OpenAI’s new voice mode makes it to the ChatGPT desktop app OpenAI on Thursday said it has updated its ChatGPT desktop app to add support for ChatGPT Voice, allowing users to talk to the app to control AI agents and perform tasks on their computer.

The new feature taps OpenAI’s new family of voice models called ChatGPT-Live , which it launched earlier this month.

OpenAI said ChatGPT Voice works with both ChatGPT Work and Codex, and can also tap computer use skills to look up websites and apps.

Plus, on macOS, with Appshots, users can let the app access what’s on their screen, including alt-text.

At launch, ChatGPT Voice’s smartphone version featured smoother conversations, with better interruption handling, but it was not built to take action on smartphones.

Thursday’s desktop update is more capable, allowing users to dictate complex commands involving many steps, and respond when ChatGPT needs their input.

In a demo video, OpenAI showed a developer asking ChatGPT to create a new thread, make a pull request, and find the root cause for a bug, with one command.

The company said that users can utilize ChatGPT Voice in Codex from the iOS app through remote access.

Anthropic has also updated its voice mode for Claude , which can tap the company’s Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models to complete tasks in apps like Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, and Canva.
